title: Pressure Washing Scheduling & Invoicing Software (2026)
description: Pressure washing scheduling and invoicing software compared: recurring jobs, rain-day rescheduling, deposits, autopay and card fees for 5 tools, with costs.
h1: Pressure washing scheduling and invoicing software: recurring jobs, rain delays and getting paid
body:
Winning the quote is half the job. The other half is everything after the customer says yes: getting the wash on the calendar, moving it when it rains, setting up the repeat house wash or storefront clean, collecting a deposit, sending the invoice before you leave and getting paid. This page compares five tools on that after-the-sale work only: recurring and seasonal scheduling, rain-delay rescheduling, deposits, invoicing, automatic payments and card fees, plus what each costs for a solo operator and a 5-person crew. Everything comes from the vendors' own pricing, pressure washing and help pages, checked 2026-11-25. Anything a vendor doesn't publish is marked unknown. For quoting tools and overall picks, see best pressure washing software and the pressure washing hub.

Prices exclude card processing, tax and add-ons. Jobber's 5-user Connect price is its published team tier. Markate's online booking form is a $10/mo add-on, so add it if customers book themselves. Several vendors were running time-limited promotions on 2026-11-25; the table uses list prices.

1. Jobber: recurring billing options and bulk rain-day rescheduling

Jobber's help center says a recurring job can repeat weekly, biweekly, monthly or on a custom schedule, and can be invoiced per visit or at a fixed price, after each visit, monthly or on a custom schedule. Its pressure washing page says you can drag a visit to a new day or bulk-reschedule a whole day of visits when weather hits, and customers get the updated time automatically. Invoices are built from the approved quote, or sent in batches. Core ($29/mo billed annually, $49/mo monthly, 1 user) covers scheduling, quotes, invoices and online payments. Automatic payments (charging a saved card for recurring work), automated reminders, invoice follow-ups and QuickBooks Online sync start on Connect ($99/mo billed annually, $139/mo monthly). Extra users are $29/mo each. Fees: 2.9% + 30¢ online, 2.7% + 30¢ Tap to Pay, ACH 1%. Sources: Jobber pricing, Jobber pressure washing page, Jobber recurring jobs help. Full breakdown: Jobber pricing. {{aff:jobber|See Jobber plans}}

2. Housecall Pro: users included, recurring service plans on MAX

Housecall Pro's pressure washing page lists one-time and recurring washes, moving rain-delayed jobs on a drag-and-drop schedule, deposits on estimates, invoices with photos and checklists sent before the crew leaves, and automatic reminders for overdue invoices. Basic is $59/mo billed annually ($79/mo monthly) for 1 user. Essentials ($149/mo annually, $189/mo monthly) includes 5 users and adds routes and QuickBooks Online sync. MAX ($299/mo annually, $329/mo monthly, 8 users) adds Recurring Service Plans for maintenance agreements and route optimization. Cards start at 2.59% and bank payments are 1%. Neither page we checked says which plan, if any, charges a card on file automatically, so that is unknown. Sources: Housecall Pro pricing, Housecall Pro pressure washing page. Full breakdown: Housecall Pro pricing. {{aff:housecallpro|See Housecall Pro plans}}

3. QuoteIQ: the most billing features on its entry plan

QuoteIQ's co-founder is a former pressure washing business owner, per its pricing page, and its plan table puts most of the after-sale work on the $29.99/mo Essentials plan (1 user): recurring jobs, recurring billing (invoice subscriptions), deposits and partial payments, card on file, tips, payment links and QR codes, card and ACH payments via Stripe or Whop, and built-in weather forecasts. Mass invoicing starts on Beginner ($99.99/mo, 2 users). Assigning jobs to team members, QuickBooks and job costing start on Pro ($199.99/mo, 4 users). Online self-scheduling and route optimization start on Elite ($299.99/mo, 10 users). Extra users are $25/mo on any plan. Annual billing is the price of 10 months. The 14-day trial needs a credit or debit card, and processing fees are separate and not listed on the pricing page. Source: QuoteIQ pricing. Compare it head to head in QuoteIQ vs Jobber. {{aff:quoteiq|Try QuoteIQ free for 14 days}}

4. Markate: low base price, $5 per employee

Markate charges $49.95/mo ($45.95/mo billed yearly, $551.40/yr) for the owner, plus $5/mo per employee, so a 5-person crew is $69.95/mo by its published formula. Its pricing page lists as included: recurring work orders, progressive and recurring invoices, bulk reassigning and rescheduling of jobs, a drag-and-drop calendar, automated invoice follow-ups, ACH and card on file through Square, Wisetack financing and a QuickBooks integration. Its pressure washing page adds capturing signatures and deposits. Several things cost extra: the online booking form ($10/mo), automated review requests ($10/mo), a branded customer portal ($10/mo) and Zapier ($10/mo). Card processing rates aren't published. The trial is 14 days with no credit card, there's no contract, and Markate doesn't refund early cancellations within a billing period. Sources: Markate pricing, Markate pressure washing page. {{aff:markate|Visit Markate}}

5. Workiz: deposits and recurring jobs on every plan, no public prices

Workiz's pricing page lists recurring jobs, estimate deposits, online payments, tap to pay and QuickBooks Online on all three plans (Standard, Pro, Ultimate). Its pressure washing page pitches service plans for recurring maintenance revenue, but the pricing page lists service plans on Ultimate only. Genius Scheduling is on Pro and Ultimate. Prices show "Request pricing" on every plan, and card rates aren't published. There's a 7-day trial with no credit card. Sources: Workiz pricing, Workiz pressure washing page. {{aff:workiz|Visit Workiz}}

How to choose

  • Lots of repeat customers (annual house washes, monthly storefronts): look for recurring jobs and automatic billing on the plan you'll pay for. Jobber charges saved cards automatically from Connect. QuoteIQ has recurring billing on Essentials. Markate includes recurring invoices in its base price. Housecall Pro's Recurring Service Plans and Workiz's service plans are top-tier only.
  • Rain days: Jobber and Markate both publish bulk rescheduling, which moves a whole day at once. QuoteIQ shows weather forecasts on the calendar. Housecall Pro describes drag-and-drop moves for rain-delayed jobs.
  • Deposits on big jobs (roofs, commercial flatwork): all five list deposits. QuoteIQ and Workiz put them on every plan.
  • Card fees: only Jobber (2.9% + 30¢ online, ACH 1%) and Housecall Pro (from 2.59%, bank 1%) publish rates. On a $400 job, Jobber's 1% ACH fee is $4, against $11.90 at its 2.9% + 30¢ online card rate.
  • QuickBooks: Jobber Connect+, Housecall Pro Essentials+, QuoteIQ Pro+, Markate included, Workiz all plans. See field service software with QuickBooks.
  • Before you pay: run one real week, including a rain-out and a recurring invoice, in the trial. Use the software buying checklist and compare prices in the pricing tracker. Window cleaners with the same questions can see window cleaning scheduling software.

faq: What is pressure washing scheduling and invoicing software?

Software that puts approved washes on a calendar, handles repeat and rescheduled visits, and turns finished jobs into invoices you can collect online. Jobber, Housecall Pro, QuoteIQ, Markate and Workiz all list scheduling, invoicing and online payments on their own pages (checked 2026-11-25).
Which pressure washing software can reschedule a whole day for rain?

Jobber's pressure washing page describes bulk rescheduling that moves a whole day of visits at once and notifies customers automatically. Markate's pricing page lists bulk reassigning and rescheduling of jobs. Housecall Pro's pressure washing page describes moving rain-delayed jobs on a drag-and-drop schedule, and QuoteIQ shows built-in weather forecasts on every plan (checked 2026-11-25).
Which tool has the cheapest recurring billing for a solo pressure washer?

QuoteIQ Essentials ($29.99/mo) lists recurring jobs, recurring billing, deposits and card on file. Markate ($49.95/mo, or $45.95/mo billed yearly) includes recurring invoices. Jobber's automatic payments for recurring work start on Connect at $99/mo billed annually or $139/mo monthly (checked 2026-11-25).
Can I take a deposit before a pressure washing job?

Yes, all five tools list deposits. QuoteIQ (deposits and partial payments) and Workiz (estimate deposits) include them on every plan. Housecall Pro lists deposits on estimates, Jobber collects deposits on approved quotes, and Markate's pressure washing page mentions capturing deposits (checked 2026-11-25).
What are the card processing fees?

Jobber publishes 2.9% + 30¢ for online cards, 2.7% + 30¢ for Tap to Pay and 1% for ACH. Housecall Pro publishes cards from 2.59% and 1% for bank payments. QuoteIQ (Stripe or Whop), Markate (Square) and Workiz don't publish their rates on the pages we checked (2026-11-25).
Workiz doesn't publish prices. Its pricing page shows 'Request pricing' for Standard, Pro and Ultimate as of 2026-11-25, with a 7-day free trial and no credit card required.
